cards.text: The apostle Paul is writing a letter to the church in Thessalonica. Some of their believers have died, and Paul calls it sleeping in death. He doesn't want the church left uninformed about them.

cards.question: Paul wants the Thessalonians informed about the believers who sleep in death. Why?

answers.text: So they won't grieve like people without hope
So they can honor them every year
So they stop talking about them

cards.text: I went YEARS without hope in a junk drawer, friend, just me collecting dust. Then Paul points the church to what they already believe: Jesus died and rose again.

cards.question: Because Jesus died and rose again, what does Paul say God will do with the believers who have fallen asleep in Him?

cards.text: Then Paul says he's declaring this by the word of the Lord. It's about the believers who are still alive and remain when that great day comes.

cards.question: Paul says the believers who are alive and remain on that day will go ahead of the ones who have fallen asleep.

cards.text: No cutting in line, and you KNOW I'd be the one trying to sneak up front! Then Paul paints the scene: a loud command, the voice of an archangel and the trumpet of God.

cards.question: With a loud command and the trumpet of God, Paul says someone will come down from heaven. Who?

cards.text: Then Paul says somebody gets to rise first, and no, friend, it's NOT me sneaking to the front.

cards.question: When the Lord comes down from heaven, who does Paul say will be the first to rise?

cards.text: After that, it's the turn of the believers who are still alive and remain.

cards.question: Paul says the living believers will be caught up together with the dead in Christ, in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air.
Once they meet the Lord in the air, how long will they be with Him? Paul says they will ___ be with the Lord.

cards.text: Then Paul tells the church what to do with everything he just wrote.

cards.question: What does Paul tell the Thessalonians to do with these words about the Lord's coming?

cards.text: Now Paul turns to the times and seasons, and he says he doesn't even need to write to them about it. They already know full well how the Day of the Lord will come.

cards.question: Paul says the church is fully aware of how the Day of the Lord will come. How?

answers.text: Like a thief in the night
Like a sunrise after a long night
Like a king with a long parade

cards.text: A thief never texts you "On my way!" first, so I skip the date guessing and just keep the ovens hot, baker. Then Paul says people will be going around talking about peace and security.

cards.question: While people are saying "Peace and security," what does Paul say happens to them?
Paul compares that sudden destruction to labor pains on a pregnant woman, and he says those people will escape it.

cards.text: Then Paul turns back to the believers in Thessalonica, and the whole picture flips.

cards.question: Paul says the Day won't overtake the Thessalonian believers like a thief. Why not?

answers.text: They are not in the darkness
They live far from the city

cards.text: Paul calls them sons of the light and sons of the day, and I spent YEARS getting two seconds of light whenever somebody dug around for the tape. These folks get to BELONG to the day?

cards.question: Since the believers belong to the day and not the night, what does Paul tell them to do?

answers.text: Rest up as much as they can
Wait for a sign in the sky

cards.text: Paul points out that sleeping and getting drunk are things people do at night. Kind of like the snooze button, which has NEVER made anybody more ready for anything.
Since they belong to the day, Paul tells them to be sober and suit up with a breastplate and a helmet. Meanwhile I'm out here in an APRON.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers to put on a breastplate. What is it made of?
Paul's armor for the believers has a helmet too. What is the helmet?

cards.text: Then Paul tells them what God has appointed them for.

cards.question: Paul says God has appointed the believers to suffer wrath.

cards.text: Not wrath, but salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ. And Paul says Jesus died for us.

cards.question: Paul says Jesus died for us so that, whether we are awake or asleep, we may live ___ with Him.

cards.text: Then Paul wraps it up a lot like he wrapped up the last part: encourage one another. But this time he adds something.

cards.question: Besides encouraging one another, what else does Paul tell the Thessalonians to do, just as they're already doing?

findings.problem: The opening card uses two facts from outside the passage: Paul is the writer, and the letter goes to the church in Thessalonica. Both come from 1 Thessalonians 1:1, but the card gives no reference for them. It cites only 1 Thessalonians 4:13.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "just me collecting dust" adds something new to his backstory and contradicts it. In the backstory he wasn't alone in the drawer: "He wasn't the only one stuck in there... They were all in it together."

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: "when that great day comes" renames what 1 Thessalonians 4:15 calls "the coming of the Lord." The passage never says "great day." The card also blends it with "the Day of the Lord," which doesn't appear until 5:2. If the text's wording would make card 8 too easy, it can still be told as "the coming of the Lord" as an easy follow-up, or card 8 can ask something else.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 5 multiple choice, 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank. The order also matches stop 2: it opens with two multiple choice and then a true or false, and it ends with the stop's only fill in the blank followed by a final multiple choice.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
